rv.q: They are supported by a tremendous company of street vendors/servants/racegoers whose individual characters shine through. Ashley Nottingham’s gloriously wild choreography for ‘Get Me to the Church on Time’ was a highlight among many rousing ensemble numbers, and Tim Hatley’s gorgeous costumes looked wonderful on aristocrats and hoi polloi alike.

Maria Friedman ’s direction contains countless little physical touches that point up the characters’ personalities and deepen the comedy, while Tim Hatley’s handsome designs serve the story with flexible sets, atmospheric stage pictures and some lovely costumes.
Visually, it’s an abso-bloomin’-lutely loverly treat.
My Fair Lady is the epitome of a timeless musical treasure; the example you would give to someone who asked, "What makes a great musical?"
The entire production is flawless from beginning to end. At almost three hours, it absolutely flies by.
Without a wretched LCD screen in sight, the lavish and painstaking recreation is a true work of beauty, all the better when blessed with such a stellar cast.
From its magnificent performances to its dazzling costumes and extraordinary staging, every element feels considered and beautifully executed.
This lavish 70th Anniversary production, presented by Opera Australia and John Frost, is a thoroughly enchanting celebration of a theatrical classic.
In the Ian Potter State Theatre, My Fair Lady has found a grand new home and stands as one of Melbourne's genuine theatre highlights of 2026.
For the cast performances and moments of elaborate set design, this show absolutely delivers.

cn.t: Critics rave about Melbourne's My Fair Lady revival, praising its dazzling production design and enduring charm. A near-unanimous hit, this 70th anniversary staging earns top marks across the board.

ta: Ian Potter State Theatre, 100 St Kilda Road, Melbourne VIC 3004
